hook.line: UK sole traders and landlords will be on Making Tax Digital by 2028.

split.title: Five filings, not one.
split.p1: Four quarterly updates of income and expenses, then a final declaration once the tax year ends.
split.p2: Records kept digitally and sent through HMRC-compatible software. A spreadsheet alone does not count.

stairs.title: Who is next?
stairs.p1: Qualifying income is gross: self-employment plus property income, before expenses.

bars.title: Your 2025/26 income decides.
bars.p1: The test uses gross income, not profit. This example is over the line.
bars.p2: That tax year ended on 5 April 2026, so your number is already fixed.

points.title: Then the points start.
points.t1: Each missed quarterly deadline earns a point. Enough points means a financial penalty.
points.t2: Early easements may not cover people joining for the first time in 2027 or 2028.

list.title: Do this before April.

items.d: Add up your 2025/26 gross income from self-employment and property.
Check whether your accountant will do the quarterly updates, and the cost.
Pick HMRC-compatible software and keep digital records from now.

list.foot: General information, not tax advice. Check dates on gov.uk.

end.tagline: We tidy your records with AI before they reach your software.
